input.message: unequip exists, and drop can let go of what you are holding
input.rationale: Malcolm, live on the quay, typed drop knife / drop clasp-knife and was told he wasn't carrying one while it was open in his hand, then unequip knife / unequip clasp-knife / unequip coat and the word wasn't recognised at all. Drop now finds equipped items and lets go first; unequip/remove/take off/sheathe/stow put a held thing back in the pack, bare or named; help teaches the opposite of the verb it already taught.
